summary.text: A 34-year-old male deceased-donor kidney transplant recipient (transplanted in 2016, with anti-thymocyte globulin induction and prednisolone, tacrolimus and mycophenolate maintenance) presented four years later with a 15-day fever without localized symptoms or signs, anaemia, thrombocytopenia, stable graft function (serum creatinine 1.3 mg/dL), sterile blood cultures and a normal abdominal ultrasound.

He was empirically treated and discharged, then readmitted a month later with intermittent fever of 39.4 °C; abdominal CT showed multiple evolving liver and spleen abscesses and aspirated liver pus grew B. pseudomallei (melioidosis). Tacrolimus trough was 5.4 ng/mL and mycophenolate AUC 38.9 mg h/L at the time of infection.

He received renal-adjusted meropenem 1 g intravenously every eight hours for 6 weeks, then oral cotrimoxazole for 3 months; repeat imaging at 3 months showed resolution of the abscesses, he continued to recover well and kept stable graft function without mortality.

summary.text: A 37-year-old woman with native kidney disease due to IgA nephropathy had a live related donor ABO compatible kidney transplant in 2018 (basiliximab induction; prednisolone, tacrolimus and mycophenolate, with mycophenolate later stopped for persistent severe leucopenia).

Six months after transplant she presented with an acute febrile illness without localising symptoms or signs; she had leucopenia, stable graft function (serum creatinine 1.5 mg/dL), normal chest and abdomen imaging, tacrolimus trough 6.7 ng/mL, and blood culture grew B. pseudomallei (melioidosis, isolated bacteremia).

She received renal-adjusted meropenem 1 g intravenously every eight hours for 4 weeks (stopped after blood cultures showed no growth), then oral cotrimoxazole for 3 months; repeat blood cultures were sterile at the end of 4 weeks with no further complications, and she kept stable graft function without mortality.
